meta.title: Agent Roster
meta.description: Static member rosters for multi-agent teams: define, validate, edit and inspect them in one panel.

settings.languageHint: The panel follows the DSH language by default; pick a language to pin it.
settings.rosterDirsHint: Empty means the global library at $DSH_HOME/agent-roster (~/.dsh/agent-roster), shared across workspaces. Only a relative path is resolved per workspace.
settings.stateDirHint: Read-only: used to compare roster values with what the runtime actually created.
settings.policiesNone: Not configured — policy ids in rosters stay declarations only.
settings.saveFailed: Could not save — the settings form is unavailable.
settings.mirrorHint: When set, this replaces the region preset for index sources published as npm packages. Company mirrors with a sub-path (e.g. /repository/npm) work too; leave empty to use the region preset.

panel.title: Agent Roster
panel.subtitle: {rosters} rosters · {members} members · {teams} teams
panel.searchPlaceholder: Filter by id, title, member or tag
panel.emptyBody: A roster is a plain YAML or JSON file under a roster directory. Create one here, or drop a file into the directory yourself.
panel.workspaceFallback: No workspace is registered yet; reading the process directory instead.
panel.tagPoolEmpty: No tags yet — add `tags:` to an archive.
panel.emptyFavoritesBody: This tab lists only the rosters you favorite. Pick a few from the library and tap the star; they show up here.

roster.copyFailed: The clipboard is unavailable; select the text instead.

team.emptyBody: Teams are created and scheduled by dsh-agent-teams. This panel only reads their state so you can tell whether a roster really landed.
team.emptyCta: Copy a team payload from a roster

editor.idHint: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore. It is also the directory name.
editor.titleHint: Shown in the panel; free text.
editor.memberScopeHint: Comma separated tool names; empty means inherit.
editor.skillsHint: Comma separated skill names. The runtime does not load them; the roster only records intent.
editor.examplesHint: One per line. Used as hints when delegating, never executed.
editor.captainHint: The captain is the session that creates a team, not a member. Record here what it should be; the profile decides the real model.
editor.captainNameHint: kebab-case. Leave empty to drop the whole captain block.
editor.captainPersonaHint: Injected verbatim into the session's kick-off prompt when applied, taking precedence there; the model still comes from the deployment.
editor.overwriteBody: {file} already exists. Saving replaces it and keeps a .bak copy next to it.
editor.emptyMembers: A roster needs at least one member.
editor.emptyMemberPrompt: Every member needs a system prompt.
editor.sourceHint: Edit the file as-is. The host validates it before writing; nothing is written when validation fails.

delete.title: Delete {id}?
delete.body: This removes {file} from the roster directory. Teams that already used it keep their members; the roster just stops describing them.

importDialog.title: Import a roster
importDialog.hint: Paste a roster document. The host validates it and writes it into the selected directory.

diagnostics.title: Health
diagnostics.intro: Everything the plugin can check about its own configuration, the rosters, and the teams they describe.
diagnostics.empty: Nothing to report: configuration, rosters and teams are consistent.

workspace-fallback.title: No workspace registered
workspace-fallback.body: DSH has not registered a workspace for this session, so roster directories were resolved against the process directory. Open a workspace so the panel reads the right files.

roster-dir-missing.title: Roster directory missing
roster-dir-missing.body: {dirSpec} does not exist under {rootDir}. Create the directory, or change roster directories in the plugin settings.

roster-dir-empty.title: Roster directory is empty
roster-dir-empty.body: {rootDir} exists but holds no roster. Add a folder with a roster.yaml inside, or create one here.

no-rosters.title: No rosters anywhere
no-rosters.body: Every configured roster directory is empty. Tools will report zero rosters until one exists.

tool-policies-unset.title: Tool policies are not verified
tool-policies-unset.body: Rosters name tool policies but the plugin does not know which ids your deployment declares. Fill known tool policies in the plugin settings to catch typos.

teams-none.title: No teams yet
teams-none.body: The team state directory {stateDir} holds no team. Rosters can still be inspected; deployment status stays unknown.

state-dir-missing.title: Team state directory missing
state-dir-missing.body: {stateDir} does not exist yet, so no team can be compared with a roster. This is normal before the first team is created.

duplicate-roster-id.title: Duplicate roster ids
duplicate-roster-id.body: {count} roster id appears in more than one directory. Tools resolve the first match only; rename one of them.

roster-errors.title: Rosters with errors
roster-errors.body: {count} error findings across the library. Those rosters cannot be used as team member sources.

captain.title: Captain
captain.hint: The captain is the session that creates the team — it has no member row. Its persona comes from the roster's captain section (injected into the session when applied); its model comes from the deployment (agent-default-model), which the plugin does not write.
captain.noChecks: No deployment config read yet — nothing to compare.
captain.applied: Applied — the team prompt is queued in that session

catalog.placeholder: What should it do? e.g. data quality, release, review
catalog.empty: Nothing matches. Try another wording, or check Sources for a subscription.
catalog.failed: The library did not load: the host did not answer.

teamCreate.title: Create a team from {roster}
teamCreate.hint: The plugin never writes team state: it queues a build prompt into the captain session, which then calls agent_teams_create and adds each member.
teamCreate.noModel: not declared, the session keeps its model
teamCreate.noCaptain: This roster has no captain block: it can still build a team, but the captain model is not switched.
teamCreate.queued: Queued into session {session} — that session will build the team.
